judged_text: The findFirst-then-create sequence runs without a transaction and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent syncs both take the create path, and the unordered findFirst thereafter updates a nondeterministic row. Overlapping initial syncs create duplicate credentials for the same user and app, and later syncs update only one of them, leaving a stale credential that booking flows can still select - producing intermittent 401s that survive every re-sync.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId }})` followed by either `update` or `create` without a transaction. That read-then-write sequence is race-prone: two concurrent requests can both observe “no row” and both attempt `create`, or one can update a different row than intended if multiple rows exist. However, the finding’s specific claim that the `Credential` model “has no unique constraint on (userId, appId)” (and thus duplicates will be created and later `findFirst` is nondeterministic) cannot be verified from this diff because no Prisma schema/migration is shown. So the concurrency concern is real and diff-grounded, but the asserted DB constraint absence/duplicate-stale-credential behavior isn’t fully provable from the provided changes alone.
